Today we're introducing Muse Ember, our smallest and most efficient model, built for complex reasoning execution and everyday agent work.

Muse Ember can carry workflows across apps, call tools in sequence, run tests and make targeted code fixes. With a 1M-token context window and native understanding of text, images, audio and video, it can also work across large document sets and varied inputs.
Today we're also bringing Muse Ember to @GoogleCloud  along with Muse Wonder and Muse Spark 1.3.

Today we're bringing specialized models trained using Muse Wonder to @Muse and Meta AI, giving users access to some of Muse Wonder's frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday life.

These specialized models include Muse Wonder's Active Memory and Active Focus, helping them stay aligned with your goals as tasks unfold:

→ Active Memory helps recognize when earlier information matters and distinguish what's still relevant from what's become stale

→ Active Focus helps recover from setbacks or find alternatives when constraints change

In Muse, the improved models show a 2.4x reduction in forgetting information critical to your goals and a 67% improvement in getting unstuck as constraints evolve. That means less repeating yourself and fewer dead ends when plans change.

In Meta AI, these improvements help it break complex problems into steps, ask sharper follow-up questions and adapt when you change direction.

During Connect, we previewed Muse Realtime Avatar, our real-time embodiment technology that turns Muse Realtime Voice into expressive, interactive avatars.

Today, we’re rolling it out in the @Muse app in the US, giving people a more natural way to engage with their personal agents.

Learn more about Muse Realtime Avatar on our research blog:

Today we published a technical report on Muse Glimmer, our 30B open-weight model built for agentic tasks on consumer hardware.

It runs at practical speeds on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU at 4-bit precision, and leads comparably-sized open models on tool use and multi-step planning.

Read about the model architecture, distillation recipe, quantization and more:

We trained our Muse foundational models, including Muse Wonder, at Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster in New Albany, Ohio.

Across a supercluster with hundreds of thousands of GPUs, even one underperforming host can slow an entire training run. We engineered Prometheus for resilience at scale, achieving 85%+ goodput on pretraining, 90%+ on reinforcement learning and ~47K GPU hours mean time between interruptions during Muse Wonder training.

We’re proud to share that Meta Omnilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has been named one of @TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026!

Meta Omnilingual ASR is a suite of models providing ASR capabilities for over 1,600 languages, including 500 low-coverage languages never before served by any ASR system.

While most ASR systems focus on a limited set of languages that are well-represented on the internet, this release marked a major step toward building a truly universal transcription system.

Learn more about it here:

We’re exploring how AI can accelerate health science research.

While AI has made significant breakthroughs in formal sciences like mathematics, health data science depends on imperfect real-world data and consequential choices about cohorts, variables, and causal assumptions.

To explore how AI can assist health researchers, we built a human-led research scaffold powered by Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder with access to 5M retrospective de-identified electronic health records and publicly available data. A cohort of medical experts used the system to conduct original research, accelerate hypothesis generation, code execution, and manuscript drafting while maintaining full authority over scientific decisions.

Today, we’re sharing 10 research manuscripts produced through this exploration, spanning cardiology, oncology, infectious disease, emergency medicine, and more.
